places.ad: 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: Newton Circus Food Centre opened in 1971 as a tourist-friendly open-air hawker centre at the Newton roundabout; rebuilt in 2006 and immortalised as the satay-and-chilli-crab feast in Crazy Rich Asians. With close to 100 stalls it placed five on the 2025 MICHELIN Bib Gourmand list — the most of any hawker centre — and is the gastronomic heart of Newton.

places.ad: 300 Thomson Road, Singapore 307653
places.w: The Redemptorist church that gave Novena its name — and its MRT station: built 1950 to a Swan & Maclaren design, eclectic-Modern with a triple-arched front pediment and circular stained-glass window, conserved in 2011, with a Gothic-style worship hall added in 2017. Its Saturday Perpetual Novena to Our Mother of Perpetual Help draws worshippers of every faith.
places.k: Catholic church; Saturday novena services are its busiest hours

places.ad: 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221
places.w: A turreted, Rhineland-castle-style clubhouse built in 1900 as the Deutsches Haus of the German Teutonia Club, confiscated in WWI, bought in 1918 by the Manasseh brothers as Goodwood Hall and opened as a hotel in 1929 — gazetted the 22nd National Monument (1989). Its café is the city's famous durian-dessert address.
places.k: National Monument; working hotel — the Tower Wing is viewable from the grounds

places.ad: 1 Mount Pleasant Road, Singapore
places.w: Singapore's first permanent police training institution, opened 1929 off Thomson Road and in use for more than eight decades until the move to the Home Team Academy in 2005; its colonial-era buildings are conserved by URA as the heritage core of the coming Mount Pleasant housing estate.
places.k: Conserved complex — view from Mount Pleasant Road; grounds under redevelopment

places.n: Tan Tock Seng Hospital Heritage Museum
places.ad: Tan Tock Seng Hospital, 11 Jalan Tan Tock Seng, Singapore 308433
places.w: Opened 2001 inside Singapore's first privately funded hospital (founded 1844 by philanthropist Tan Tock Seng 'for the sick poor of all nations'): artefacts, old medical equipment and a time capsule trace its fights against tuberculosis in the 1940s and SARS in 2003.
places.k: Small free museum inside the hospital

places.ad: Lornie Road / Kheam Hock Road, Novena, Singapore
places.w: Singapore's largest Chinese cemetery and reputedly the largest outside China: ~100,000 graves on 70–86 ha of overgrown hills, opened as a municipal cemetery on 1 Jan 1922 and closed to burials in 1973. Grand Peranakan and Hokkien tombs with Sikh guardian statues and tiled tablets; partly exhumed in 2012–13 for a highway, which sparked a heritage campaign that now runs free guided walks.
places.k: Free; join a Brownies heritage walk (weekends); bring insect repellent

places.ad: Cairnhill Road, Newton, Singapore
places.w: A former nutmeg plantation turned early-1900s residential quarter for the wealthy, conserved by URA on 7 Jul 1989: a stretch of mostly two-storey Late and Art Deco-style terrace houses raised above the road on flights of steps, with recessed verandahs and geometric ventilation blocks — several restorations have won URA Architectural Heritage Awards. On NHB's Orchard Heritage Trail, which also points out the c.1926 Tan Chin Tuan Mansion with its bell-shaped turret.
places.k: Free; private homes — view from the street

places.ad: 42 Cairnhill Road, Singapore
places.w: A 1926 mansion at the junction of Cairnhill Road and Cairnhill Circle, built in the rubber-boom era and later home of OCBC chairman and philanthropist Tan Chin Tuan — note the tower with its bell-shaped turret and the columned porch. Conserved by URA and pointed out on NHB's Orchard Heritage Trail; now fronting a condominium.

places.ad: #01-28 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A Newton fixture since 1971 and a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand stall: the owner has 50+ years at the wok and still steams the radish cake in-house rather than buying it factory-made, frying black and white versions (plus oyster omelette) with vegetable oil only — no pork or lard.

places.ad: #01-13 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A 40-year-old braised-duck stall whose boneless, herbal-braised duck — over rice, congee or noodles — earned back-to-back MICHELIN Bib Gourmand listings (2023–2025); one of five Newton stalls that made the 2025 Bib list, the most of any hawker centre.

places.ad: #01-20 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A 60-year-old Teochew fish-porridge stall now run by the second generation — fresh-sliced fish in a clean broth, as porridge or soup — MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2021–2023 and on Seth Lui's Newton best-of (Oct 2024 update).

places.n: Newton Old Signboard 25 Fried Hokkien Prawn Noodle
places.ad: #01-25 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: Newton's Hokkien mee benchmark: a smoky, lard-laced tangle of bee hoon and yellow noodles simmered down in a generous prawn stock — singled out by Eatbook for its wok hei and reviewed by the Ordinary Patrons blog.

places.n: Bee Heng Satay, BBQ Prawn & Otah
places.ad: #01-12 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: The family business behind Bee Heng Popiah (founded 1930, at Newton since 1977, now third-generation Gary Tan) — long Newton's resident popiah roll, written up by ieatishootipost and Miss Tam Chiak; since 2023 the stall has stopped the popiah and trades as Bee Heng Satay, BBQ Prawn & Otah.

places.ad: Goldhill Plaza, Thomson Road (Novena), Singapore (unit + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: An underrated Italian dining room in Goldhill Plaza by Novena — pricey, but the pasta plates earn it and the tiramisu is the one people come back for; a constant on Novena lists from Lady Iron Chef (2018) to Seth Lui and Honeycombers.

places.ad: #01-10 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: Bak chor mee given a luxe twist with XO sauce — one of the Newton stalls that the local food press point to beyond the tourist seafood row (Daniel Food Diary's 12 Newton stalls; City Nomads' 8-stall guide).

places.n: 88 San Ren Cold and Hot Dessert
places.ad: Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495 (unit to confirm)
places.w: The dessert stop to end a Newton supper — a broad board of hot and cold Chinese sweets — listed by both Eatbook and Daniel Food Diary in their Newton Food Centre guides.

places.ad: #01-31 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: One of Newton's evening barbecue-seafood stalls, picked out by both Seth Lui's 16-best (Oct 2024 update) and Eatbook's 15-best Newton guides.

places.n: Alma by Juan Amador (Goodwood Park Hotel)
places.ad: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221
places.w: The one-MICHELIN-Star contemporary European dining room inside the Goodwood Park Hotel — Juan Amador's restaurant, and the starred table of the Newton/Scotts Road edge.

places.ad: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221
places.w: The Goodwood Park's old-school grill room, a MICHELIN Selected address famous for its meat trolley carved at the table.

places.ad: Balmoral Plaza, 271 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore
places.w: A family-run retro American fast-food diner serving for more than three decades — fried chicken with Belgian waffles, burgers — that Lady Iron Chef, Seth Lui and Eatbook all describe as a time-travel back to the '80s; listed in Honeycombers' Newton guide.

places.ad: #01-83 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: One of Newton's most popular Muslim stalls: homely halal Malay nasi padang in generous servings, 6am-3pm daily — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak and listed in Eatbook's 15 best Newton stalls (Seth Lui has covered it too).

places.ad: Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495 (unit to confirm: guides print #01-44 and #01-57)
places.w: A North Indian stall with a 113-dish menu, at Newton for years — in both Seth Lui's 16 best (Oct 2024) and Eatbook's 15 best Newton stalls.

places.ad: #01-33 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: Satay since 1998: juicy charcoal-grilled chicken, mutton and pork sticks dunked in chunky peanut sauce, plus prawn satay, BBQ wings and otah — evenings from 4pm; on Eatbook's 15 best Newton stalls and Daniel Food Diary's 12 Newton stalls.

places.ad: #01-11 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A Newton barbecue-seafood stall since 1983, now run by the third generation — sambal stingray and grilled seafood (Honeycombers' Newton guide; Daniel Food Diary's Newton stalls).

places.ad: 173 Thomson Road, Goldhill Plaza, Singapore (unit to confirm)
places.w: A quiet specialty-coffee stop for Novena office workers and students, with all-day breakfast — on Lady Iron Chef's Novena/Goldhill guides and Seth Lui's Novena & Thomson must-tries.

places.ad: Royal Square at Novena, 103 Irrawaddy Road, #02-07, Singapore
places.w: A Bangkok family's first overseas outpost (they run seven restaurants at home): home-style Thai cooking with many Northern Thai recipes, steamed sea bass and most dishes under $10 — reviewed by Seth Lui and Daniel Food Diary, and on Lady Iron Chef's Novena guide.

places.ad: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
places.w: Goodwood Park's Sichuan-Cantonese dining room since 1982 — one of Singapore's most respected Chinese restaurants (Frommer's), famous for its wood-fired Beijing duck carved at the table and served in two courses; refurbished in 2020 with Ernesto Bedmar interiors. Reviewed by critic Andy Hayler.

places.n: Goodwood Park Hotel Coffee Lounge (durian desserts)
places.ad: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore
places.w: The hotel coffee lounge behind Singapore's best-known durian desserts: the Mao Shan Wang mousse cake, crêpes and Swiss rolls sold year-round and a seasonal all-you-can-eat durian dessert buffet each mid-year — covered annually by Eatbook and Time Out, and a long-running SGFoodOnFoot favourite.

places.ad: Shangri-La Singapore, Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
places.w: Singapore's oldest hotel-run Chinese restaurant, opened with the Shangri-La in 1971 in Newton's Orange Grove: a Chinese-garden dining room serving an extensive menu of old-time Cantonese classics hard to find elsewhere — featured by the MICHELIN Guide among its business-lunch picks; the dim sum menu is the affordable way in (Ordinary Patrons, 2024).

places.n: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips (Balmoral Plaza)
places.ad: Balmoral Plaza, 271 Bukit Timah Road #01-02, Singapore
places.w: Since 2006, two British founders have run what they call Singapore's only true British chippy: UK-imported cod and haddock in the founder's grandfather's 1950s batter, plus cottage pie and the deep-fried Mars bar — reviewed by Eatbook, Seth Lui, City Nomads and Time Out.

places.ad: Shangri-La Singapore, Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
places.w: The Shangri-La's lobby-level grill specialising in carefully selected grilled meats and line-caught seafood — grass- and grain-fed Australian and Irish Angus and wagyu, and exclusive snow-aged full-blood wagyu from Niigata — reviewed by The Peak, Honeycombers and SGFoodOnFoot.

places.ad: Shangri-La Singapore, 22 Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
places.w: The Shangri-La's garden-and-pool-view buffet since 2005 — sixteen live stations from sushi, sashimi and seafood on ice to dim sum, Indian curries, made-to-order roti prata, a noodle bar and Singaporean hawker staples; Miss Tam Chiak calls it the buffet to be at, and it's reviewed by Seth Lui and Time Out.

places.ad: #01-53 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A halal-certified Newton BBQ-seafood stall whose sambal stingray — fleshy fish under heaps of smoky, fiery hei bee sambal, with chinchalok and lime on the side — Miss Tam Chiak rates among the best in the centre; also does lala in thick chilli-crab sauce. Named in Eatbook's Newton guide.

places.ad: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221
places.w: Goodwood Park's poolside café, a byword for elegant teatime since 1968: a daily English afternoon tea buffet of dainty sandwiches, savouries, pastries, a chocolate fountain and traditional scones — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui, Little Day Out and SGFoodOnFoot (2022).

places.ad: Shangri-La Singapore, 22 Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
places.w: A garden-set Italian at the Shangri-La, now cooking the Southern Italian dishes of chef de cuisine Simone Loisi's home region of Puglia — handmade pastas and fresh seafood; reviewed by TheSmartLocal and ladyironchef, and revisited by SGFoodOnFoot in July 2025.

places.n: Soon Wah Fishball Kway Teow Mee (Newton)
places.ad: #01-69 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: A Newton fixture since 1977 (started at an Orchard carpark in 1966): big, springy fishballs and fish dumplings hand-made daily, over mee pok tossed in chilli and vinegar — an evening-only stall picked by Daniel Food Diary's 12 Newton stalls and reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak.

places.n: Newton Tian Xiang Big Prawn Noodle
places.ad: #01-60 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: Newton's prawn-mee specialist: a deep, prawn-shell-and-pork broth poured over springy noodles with giant prawns and fall-apart pork ribs — reviewed by Seth Lui and named in Daniel Food Diary's and HungryGoWhere's Newton stall guides.

places.ad: #01-76 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, Singapore 229495
places.w: The Newton supper stall for charcoal-grilled chicken wings — glossy, smoky and cheap, with a fiery house chilli, grilling until 3am; reviewed by Daniel Food Diary (and on its 12 Newton stalls list) and in HungryGoWhere's Newton guide.

places.ad: #01-08 United Square, 101 Thomson Road, Novena
places.w: Founded 1987; a consistent big-name chicken rice institution ranked by Eatbook & Seth Lui.

places.ad: #01-73 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
places.w: Juicy-oyster orh luak with crispy edges; new Michelin Bib Gourmand.

places.ad: #01-91 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
places.w: Comforting Teochew fish porridge with deboned mackerel; new to the 2025 Michelin Bib list.

places.ad: #01-27 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
places.w: Newton's iconic sambal stingray & satay hub, featured in Crazy Rich Asians.
